metaDescription: Five slim over-the-range microwaves compared on cavity size, hood CFM, sensor cooking and smart control for kitchens with low cabinets.
expertTake: The GE Profile low profile model is the best pick because its 400 CFM fan and integrated handle make a slim body feel like a real hood. The Cosmo is the value choice with sensor cook and 11 power levels. Anyone who fries often should skip all of them and buy a dedicated ducted range hood.
introParagraphs: A low-profile microwave is a slim over-the-range unit built to fit where a standard microwave would crowd a cooktop or hit a cabinet. It combines a cooking oven and a vent fan in a shorter body, which helps in kitchens with low upper cabinets or tall cooks.

The tradeoff for the slim design is a smaller cavity and a vent fan that has to work harder in a tighter space. Hood strength, sensor cooking and install effort matter more than headline wattage here, and this guide compares them across the five distinct models.

products.name: GE Profile 30 in 1.2 cu ft 1000W low profile over-the-range microwave
products.description:
GE Profile designs this to fit in the same space as a regular undercabinet hood, which is the whole point of a low profile. The body is slim, the handle is integrated into the bottom, and the front stays smooth and easy to wipe. The 400 CFM vent is the strongest listed in this lineup, and LED lighting brightens the cooktop.

The cavity is 1.2 cubic feet at 1000 watts, which fits a dinner plate and a medium bowl but not a wide casserole. Auto cook options reduce guesswork. Next to the Midea, you gain a stronger fan and the Profile styling, and you pay for it.

Install it as you would any over-the-range unit: a stud-mounted bracket, an outlet above the range and a vent path for ducted setups. Wash the grease filters monthly because the fan pulls oil off the cooktop. For kitchens with low cabinets, it is the one to buy. The auto cook options cover the usual snack list, so most of the daily work is one button. Compared with the Cosmo, you pay for the stronger fan and for a brand with a deeper service network.
products.bestFor: Kitchens with low cabinets that want a strong vent and clean styling.
pros: 400 CFM vent is the strongest here
Low profile fits under tight cabinets
cons: Higher cost than the budget slim units
Needs stud mounting and an outlet above

products.name: Samsung 1.1 cu ft smart SLIM over-the-range microwave with 550 CFM vent
products.description:
Samsung's SLIM microwave leads on ventilation, with a 550 CFM fan listed. A strong fan matters because a slim body sits close to the cooktop and has less room to capture steam. Wi-Fi and voice control add app starts and hands-free commands, and an LED light bar illuminates the burners.

The cavity is 1.1 cubic feet, the smallest in this lineup, so tall dishes and wide plates are a tighter fit. You are paying for fan power and smart control rather than size. Compared with the GE Profile, the Samsung moves more air but holds a bit less food.

Smart features depend on Wi-Fi and app support, and the oven still works as a normal microwave without them. Keep the filters clean and plan the install carefully. It suits cooks who want a strong hood from a slim body. If your ductwork is long, a high CFM rating helps recover the airflow lost in elbows. Owners with a short, straight run get the full benefit, so check the duct path before paying for fan power.
products.bestFor: Cooks who prioritize a strong 550 CFM fan and smart control in a slim body.
pros: 550 CFM vent is the strongest listed
LED light bar brightens the cooktop
cons: 1.1 cu ft is the smallest cavity here
Higher cost for the fan and connectivity

products.name: Cosmo COS-3012ORLP1SS 30 in 1.2 cu ft 1000W slim over-the-range microwave

specList.label: Auto cook
specList.value: 7 options including sensor cook and reheat

products.description:
Cosmo packs eleven power levels and seven auto cook options into a slim 1.2 cubic foot over-the-range body. Sensor cook and sensor reheat reduce guesswork, and defrost works by weight or by time. At 1000 watts it matches the GE Profile for speed.

The feature list is generous for a unit that sits in the lower price tier of this lineup, and the stainless finish blends with other appliances. Cosmo is a smaller brand than GE or Samsung, so service reach is narrower. Check the warranty terms and where you would get parts.

Install it with a stud bracket and an outlet above, and wash the filters regularly. It suits buyers who want the slim shape and sensors without paying for premium branding. Defrosting by weight is a useful tool for meat, because the oven sets the time from the load. Keep an eye on filter cleaning, since that upkeep is the same no matter the price.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want sensors and eleven power levels in a slim body.
pros: Eleven power levels for fine control
Lower cost than GE and Samsung
cons: Fan strength is not published as high as rivals

products.name: Midea 1.2 cu ft 1000W slim low profile over-the-range microwave

specList.label: Control
specList.value: SmartHome app for cooking and venting

products.description:
Midea lets you control both cooking and ventilation from an app, and it notifies you when a cycle finishes. The slim body frees overhead space, a 400 CFM fan handles the cooktop, and sensor cook adjusts time to the food. Output is 1000 watts in a 1.2 cubic foot cavity.

App control of the fan is the more unusual feature, since it lets you start ventilation as you begin cooking. The Midea matches the GE Profile on fan rating, but it is a less familiar brand in the service world.

Use the filters as directed and clean them monthly. The app works only with a stable connection, so it is a bonus rather than a necessity. It suits tech-comfortable cooks. Starting the fan from the app before you light a burner is a small habit that keeps steam off the cabinets. Without the app, you still have the manual controls, so a dead Wi-Fi link does not stop dinner.
products.bestFor: Cooks who like starting the hood fan and the oven from an app.
pros: 400 CFM fan matches the GE Profile
cons: Midea has a smaller service reach

products.name: ThermoMate 30 in 1.2 cu ft 1000W low profile over-the-range microwave
products.description:
ThermoMate pairs a slim over-the-range body with smart sensor auto-cook and voice control. The sensor adjusts time and power from the food's moisture, and one-touch buttons start common jobs. It takes up much less space than a standard over-the-range microwave.

Output is 1000 watts in a 1.2 cubic foot cavity, the same as the Cosmo and Midea. Voice control is handy with full hands, though it may depend on a smart speaker or app. Brand reach is narrow compared with GE or Samsung.

Install it with a stud bracket and keep the filters clean. It is an affordable slim option with sensor and voice features. Because the brand is newer to the category, keep your proof of purchase and photos of the installation in case a warranty claim comes up. Next to the Cosmo, it trades the eleven power levels for voice control.
products.bestFor: Shoppers who want sensor cooking and voice control at a modest cost.
pros: Sensor auto-cook adjusts time and power
cons: No published fan rating in the listing

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Samsung lists 550 CFM and the GE Profile and Midea list 400 CFM, which is a real gap in how quickly steam leaves the cooktop. A slim body leaves less room under the unit, so a strong fan matters more than on a standard model. A fan rated 300 CFM or less handles boiling but struggles with searing. Check the duct path too, since a long run with elbows cuts real airflow. A short straight duct to the outside gives the most of the rated number. Recirculating setups filter the air and return it, which lowers smoke removal further.

Low profile bodies are short, so the cavity shrinks to 1.1 or 1.2 cubic feet. The Samsung at 1.1 cubic feet is the tightest, and the GE Profile, Cosmo, Midea and ThermoMate sit at 1.2. A 1.2 cubic foot cavity fits a dinner plate but may not clear a tall bowl. Measure your biggest dish before you choose a slim unit. Also check the turntable diameter, since a short cabinet often pairs with a smaller tray. If you reheat wide platters, a standard over-the-range unit may suit you better.

A low profile unit is chosen to fit a tight gap between cooktop and cabinet. Codes set a minimum clearance above the cooktop, so confirm the installation height in the manual. Hanging it too low makes back burners awkward. A unit that is too high is also awkward to reach. Measure from the cooktop surface to the cabinet bottom, not from the floor. Leave margin for the bracket plate, which adds depth to the wall.

The Cosmo, Midea and ThermoMate list sensor cook, and the Cosmo adds sensor reheat. Sensors read steam to set time and power. Covered dishes can fool them, so stir and rest food regardless. Heat from the cooktop below can also warm the cavity, which is one more reason to let the oven settle between cycles. Sensor reheat is the most useful mode for leftovers.

The Samsung adds Wi-Fi and voice control, the Midea controls cooking and the fan by app, and the ThermoMate offers voice control. Smart layers depend on connectivity and app support. They are bonuses, not reasons to overpay. Ask yourself whether you would use an app to start a fan, and whether your router reaches the kitchen. If not, a plain model with good sensors is the better spend.

GE and Samsung have the widest service reach, while Cosmo, Midea and ThermoMate are narrower. A microwave mounted above a range is hard to swap, so repair access matters. Check the warranty and parts supply before you commit. Filters, bulbs and control boards are the parts you may need within a few years. A lower price is not a bargain if a repair means replacing the whole unit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Form factor purity
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept only slim over-the-range units and skipped countertop models that appeared in related searches. That left five distinct machines. Low profile was judged by listed body and cavity size.

howWeEvaluated.title: Venting
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared CFM ratings from the spec sheets. The Samsung lists 550, and the GE Profile and Midea list 400. A strong fan was weighted heavily because the slim body leaves less room.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cavity and power
howWeEvaluated.description: Our comparison covered cubic feet and output watts. All five sit at 1.1 to 1.2 cu ft, and four list 1000 W. Plate fit was weighted above volume.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cooking aids
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted sensor cook, smart control and presets. The Cosmo, Midea and ThermoMate list sensors, and the Samsung adds Wi-Fi. Aids that reduce guesswork scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership signals
howWeEvaluated.description: Long-term owner notes lean toward touch pads, latches and magnetrons as wear points. Over-the-range models were flagged for installation difficulty and filter upkeep.

rows: Sensor and voice at low cost

cards.label: Strong fan
cards.text: The Samsung moves the most air at 550 CFM but offers 1.1 cu ft. It suits kitchens where smoke is the main issue. It limits dish size.

cards.label: Big cavity
cards.text: The GE Profile, Cosmo, Midea and ThermoMate give 1.2 cu ft with 400 CFM or less. They suit cooks who reheat larger dishes. They are weaker on smoke.

howToChoose.note: Pick the Samsung for smoke. Pick a 1.2 cu ft model for dishes.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Low cabinets need a slim body, a legal cooktop clearance and a fan strong enough to clear steam in a tight space. A shorter unit helps both fit and reach.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The GE Profile fits where a hood would and offers 400 CFM. The Samsung adds more airflow when cooktop smoke is the worry.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cook with heat and smoke daily or want strong service support. The GE Profile and Samsung earn their cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly boil and reheat. The Cosmo or ThermoMate give a slim shape and sensors for less.

maintenance.why: The fan pulls oil from the cooktop. Clogged filters cut airflow and become a fire risk.
Leftover splatter takes in energy and can cause hot spots. Wipe while warm.
Residue on the seal can stop the door closing fully. Use mild soap.
A stuck damper rattles and cuts airflow. Clear it of grease.
LED or bulb lighting over the cooktop wears out. Replace per the manual.

faq.q: What makes a microwave low profile?
faq.a: It is a shorter over-the-range body that fits where a standard undercabinet hood would. The tradeoff is a smaller cavity and a slimmer vent assembly. It is built for kitchens where a standard over-the-range unit would crowd the cabinets. Most slim models list 1.1 to 1.2 cubic feet.
If your cabinets are low or you want an unobtrusive look, yes. If you need a big cavity or heavy frying, a standard unit or a ducted hood works better.

It handles steam and light smoke from boiling and sauteing. Heavy frying overwhelms it. A 550 CFM unit like the Samsung helps, but a dedicated hood is stronger. Run the fan a few minutes before and after cooking to clear lingering steam. Clean filters keep the rated airflow.

It needs a stud-mounted bracket, an outlet above the range and often a helper to lift. Many owners hire an installer. Follow the manual's clearance rules. A bracket that misses a stud can fail under the unit's weight. Use a stud finder and the supplied template, and have a helper hold the unit while you drive the fasteners.

faq.q: Do slim microwaves cook as well?
faq.a: The cooking hardware is the same as a regular 1000 watt oven. The difference is cavity size. Expect to use smaller dishes, and plan on stirring tall bowls by hand. A slim cabinet also leaves less headroom above the tray.

faq.q: How long do over-the-range microwaves last?
faq.a: Typical service life runs to several years, with touch pads, fans and magnetrons as common failures. Cleaning filters and seals helps.
